chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sabbah Al-Hazza', from Sama'ah, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). He prayed Dhuhr and Asr in front of me, and I sat with him until Maghrib time arrived. He called for ablution (wudu) and performed ablution for the prayer, then said to me, 'Perform ablution.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, I am already upon my ablution.' He said, 'Even if you are upon an ablution. Indeed, whoever performs ablution for Maghrib, that ablution is an expiation for what has passed of his sins during his day, except for the major sins. And whoever performs ablution for Fajr (the morning prayer), that ablution of his is an expiation for what has passed of his sins during his night, except for the major sins.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of performing ablution specifically for the Maghrib and Fajr prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual merit of renewing ablution specifically for the Maghrib and Fajr prayers, even when already in a state of purity. This practice serves as an expiation (kaffarah) for minor sins committed during the day and night respectively, excluding major sins, highlighting the transformative power of ritual purity in daily worship. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuous purification of the soul through repeated acts of devotion.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from one of our companions, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Sabbah Al Haza’a, from Sama’at who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Al-Hassanasws. So heasws prayed Al-Zohar and Al-Asr Salaats in front of me, and I sat in hisasws present until the Maghrib Salaat presented itself. So heasws called for the Ablution (Wudhu) and heasws performed the Ablution (Wudhu) for the Salaat, then said to me: ‘Perform Ablution (Wudhu)’. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! I am already upon my Ablution (Wudhu)’’. So heasws said: ‘And even if you were upon an Ablution (Wudhu). It is from the reverence of the Maghrib (Salaat) is its Ablution (Wudhu). That would be an expiation for whatever has passed from his sins during his day, except for the major sins. And the one who perform Ablution (Wudhu) for the morning (Salaat), that Ablution (Wudhu) of his would be an expiation for whatever had passed from his sins during his night except for the major sins’.
en.sarwar: 9. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from certain persons of our people from ’Isma‘il ibn Mehran from Sabbah al-ffadhdha’ from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“I once was in the presence of abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he (the Imam) performed al-Dhuhr and al-‘Asr Salah (prayer) before me. I remained in his presence until al-Maghrib. He (the Imam) asked for Wudu’ (water) and he took Wudu’ for al-Maghrib Salah (prayer), then said to me, ‘You need to take Wudu’. 5 I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, my Wudu’ is still valid.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Even so you should take Wudu’; to those who take Wudu’ for al-Maghrib it serves as expiation for the sins that they may have done during that day except the major sins. Taking Wudu’ in the morning serves as expiation for the sins that one had committed during the night before except the major sins.’”
